questions.subject: physics
questions.question: 1000 identical drops of oil of density 500 kg/m³ have a total mass of 5 × 10⁻⁴ kg. One drop forms a thin film of area 0.5 m² on water. What is the film thickness?
questions.ai_explanation: One drop has mass (5 × 10⁻⁴)/1000 = 5 × 10⁻⁷ kg. Its volume is m/ρ = 10⁻⁹ m³. Film thickness = volume/area = 10⁻⁹/0.5 = 2 × 10⁻⁹ m.
questions.explanation: One drop has mass (5 × 10⁻⁴)/1000 = 5 × 10⁻⁷ kg. Its volume is m/ρ = 10⁻⁹ m³. Film thickness = volume/area = 10⁻⁹/0.5 = 2 × 10⁻⁹ m.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A spring has total length 14 cm when a mass of 20 g is hung from it, and length 16 cm when a mass of 30 g is hung from it. Calculate the unstretched length, assuming Hooke’s law is obeyed.
questions.ai_explanation: Hooke’s law makes extension proportional to load. An extra 10 g increases the length by 2 cm, so the 20 g load produces a 4 cm extension. The natural length is 14 − 4 = 10 cm.
questions.explanation: Hooke’s law makes extension proportional to load. An extra 10 g increases the length by 2 cm, so the 20 g load produces a 4 cm extension. The natural length is 14 − 4 = 10 cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which statement is correct? I. Mass number equals the total number of protons and electrons in an atom. II. Atomic number equals the number of protons in an atom. III. The number of electrons in an atom equals the total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
questions.ai_explanation: Atomic number is the number of protons, so II is correct. Mass number counts protons plus neutrons. A neutral atom has equal numbers of electrons and protons, not protons plus neutrons.
questions.explanation: Atomic number is the number of protons, so II is correct. Mass number counts protons plus neutrons. A neutral atom has equal numbers of electrons and protons, not protons plus neutrons.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A current of 3 A flows for 10 seconds through a 20 Ω heating element embedded in 1000 g of oil, raising the oil temperature by 10 °C. Assuming the electrical energy heats the oil, what is its specific heat capacity?
questions.ai_explanation: Electrical energy supplied is I²Rt = 3² × 20 × 10 = 1800 J. Using Q = mcΔT, c = 1800/(1000 × 10) = 0.18 J/(g·°C), equivalent to 180 J/(kg·°C).
questions.explanation: Electrical energy supplied is I²Rt = 3² × 20 × 10 = 1800 J. Using Q = mcΔT, c = 1800/(1000 × 10) = 0.18 J/(g·°C), equivalent to 180 J/(kg·°C).

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A cell has an open-circuit terminal voltage of 2.2 V. When a 4 Ω resistor is connected across it, the terminal voltage falls to 2.0 V. What is the internal resistance?
questions.ai_explanation: The current through the external resistor is I = 2/4 = 0.5 A. The internal voltage drop is 2.2 − 2.0 = 0.2 V, so internal resistance r = 0.2/0.5 = 0.40 Ω.
questions.explanation: The current through the external resistor is I = 2/4 = 0.5 A. The internal voltage drop is 2.2 − 2.0 = 0.2 V, so internal resistance r = 0.2/0.5 = 0.40 Ω.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: QR is a vertical straight conductor, with Q above R. Current flows upwards from R to Q. Point P lies south of the wire in a horizontal plane. What is the direction of the magnetic field at P due to this current?
questions.ai_explanation: Point your right thumb upwards along the current. Your curled fingers show the magnetic-field direction around the wire. At a point south of the wire the tangent to this circle points east, so the field at P is eastwards.
questions.explanation: Point your right thumb upwards along the current. Your curled fingers show the magnetic-field direction around the wire. At a point south of the wire the tangent to this circle points east, so the field at P is eastwards.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the energy changes which take place when a steam engine drives a generator which lights a lamp?

options.C: Heat → kinetic energy → electricity → heat and light

questions.ai_explanation: The steam engine changes thermal energy into mechanical motion. The generator changes that motion into electrical energy, and the lamp changes electrical energy into light and heat.
questions.explanation: The steam engine changes thermal energy into mechanical motion. The generator changes that motion into electrical energy, and the lamp changes electrical energy into light and heat.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A horizontal copper–steel bimetallic strip is fixed at its left end P and free at its right end Q. Copper is above steel. A fixed contact is just above Q; the battery, bell, fixed contact and strip form a series circuit with an open gap at Q. The linear expansivities are 2.0 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹ for copper and 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹ for steel. Which statements describe the switching action on heating? I. The arrangement bends away from the contact and cannot close the gap. II. The arrangement bends towards the contact and closes the gap. III. Interchanging the metal layers makes the strip bend towards the contact, allowing the gap to close.
questions.ai_explanation: Copper expands more than steel, so it becomes the outside of the bend. With copper above steel, the free end bends downwards towards the steel side, away from the contact above. Reversing the layers makes it bend upwards, allowing contact. Thus I and III are correct.
questions.explanation: Copper expands more than steel, so it becomes the outside of the bend. With copper above steel, the free end bends downwards towards the steel side, away from the contact above. Reversing the layers makes it bend upwards, allowing contact. Thus I and III are correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following may be used to determine relative humidity in a physics laboratory? I Manometer II Wet-and-dry bulb hygrometer III Hair hygrometer IV A hydrometer
questions.ai_explanation: A wet-and-dry bulb hygrometer uses evaporative cooling to determine humidity. A hair hygrometer uses the change in hair length with humidity. A manometer measures pressure; a hydrometer measures liquid density.
questions.explanation: A wet-and-dry bulb hygrometer uses evaporative cooling to determine humidity. A hair hygrometer uses the change in hair length with humidity. A manometer measures pressure; a hydrometer measures liquid density.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In a vertical side view, a thin rod PQ lies horizontally on a table. A plane mirror RS slopes downwards to the right, making 45° with the horizontal. Its reflecting face is towards the rod and the observer T, who is to the left of the mirror. What is the orientation of the image of the rod?
questions.ai_explanation: Reflection in a plane mirror preserves length and reverses the component perpendicular to the mirror. Reflecting a horizontal line in a line inclined at 45° changes its orientation to vertical. The image is finite and the same size as the rod.
questions.explanation: Reflection in a plane mirror preserves length and reverses the component perpendicular to the mirror. Reflecting a horizontal line in a line inclined at 45° changes its orientation to vertical. The image is finite and the same size as the rod.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The speed of light in a vacuum is 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s. If a transparent liquid has refractive index 4/3, what is the speed of light in the liquid?
questions.ai_explanation: The refractive index is n = c/v. Therefore v = (3.0 × 10⁸)/(4/3) = 2.25 × 10⁸ m/s.
questions.explanation: The refractive index is n = c/v. Therefore v = (3.0 × 10⁸)/(4/3) = 2.25 × 10⁸ m/s.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A charge of 0.2 C experiences a force of 4 N in an electric field. What is the electric field strength?
questions.ai_explanation: Electric field strength is force per unit charge: E = F/q = 4/0.2 = 20 N/C.
questions.explanation: Electric field strength is force per unit charge: E = F/q = 4/0.2 = 20 N/C.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Longitudinal waves do not exhibit

questions.explanation: Polarization requires vibrations perpendicular to the direction of travel. Longitudinal waves vibrate along their direction of travel, so they cannot be polarized.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An inverted U-tube passes over the rim of an open water tank. Its inlet O is submerged below the water surface W; its other end P is outside the tank and open to the air. For ordinary siphon flow from the tank, which listed conditions are required?

options.A: The tube is completely filled with water and P is higher than W
options.B: P is lower than both O and W
options.C: P is lower than W and O reaches the tank bottom
options.D: The tube is completely filled with water and P is lower than W
options.E: The tube is completely filled with water and O reaches the tank bottom

questions.ai_explanation: A continuous water column must first fill the tube, and the outlet P must be below the tank’s water surface W for gravity to drive outward flow. The inlet O only needs to remain submerged; it need not reach the bottom, and P need not be lower than O.
questions.explanation: A continuous water column must first fill the tube, and the outlet P must be below the tank’s water surface W for gravity to drive outward flow. The inlet O only needs to remain submerged; it need not reach the bottom, and P need not be lower than O.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A uniform metre rule PT is horizontal and pivoted at R, its 70 cm mark. A downward force of 0.1 N acts at Q, the 60 cm mark, and a downward force of 0.4 N acts at S, the 85 cm mark. The rule is in equilibrium under these forces, its weight and the pivot reaction. What is its weight?
questions.ai_explanation: The uniform rule’s weight W acts at 50 cm, 20 cm left of the pivot. Taking moments about 70 cm gives 0.4 × 15 = 0.1 × 10 + W × 20, with distances in centimetres. Thus W = (6 − 1)/20 = 0.25 N.

questions.question: For which quantities are the dimensions ML²T⁻² correct? I. Moment of a force. II. Work. III. Acceleration.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: What volume of alcohol of density 8.4 × 10² kg/m³ has the same mass as 4.2 m³ of petrol of density 7.2 × 10² kg/m³?

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Two cells, each of emf 1.5 V and internal resistance 2 Ω, are connected in parallel with matching polarities. What current flows through an external 1 Ω resistor?

questions.ai_explanation: In a standing wave, adjacent nodes are half a wavelength apart. An antinode is midway between them, so a node and its nearest antinode are one-quarter wavelength apart.

questions.question: Two identical tuning forks have natural frequency 256 Hz. One is loaded, and 4 beats per second are heard when they sound together. What is the frequency of the loaded fork?
questions.ai_explanation: Adding a small load to a tuning fork lowers its frequency. The beat frequency is the difference between the two frequencies, so the loaded fork vibrates at 256 − 4 = 252 Hz.

questions.question: The lower (0 °C) and upper (100 °C) fixed points of a mercury-in-glass thermometer are 210 mm apart. In a room, the mercury ends 49 mm above the lower point. What is the room temperature to one decimal place?

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Between terminals X and Y, a 4 μF capacitor connects X to an intermediate node. From that node to Y are three parallel branches containing a 4 μF, a 3 μF and a 2 μF capacitor respectively. What is the effective capacitance between X and Y?

options.E: Reluctance to start moving and its reluctance to stop moving once it has begun to move.

questions.question: In a gas experiment, the pressure of the gas is plotted against the reciprocal of the volume of the gas at a constant temperature. The unit of the slope of the resulting curve is

questions.explanation: Slope is pressure divided by reciprocal volume, so its units are pressure × volume: (N/m²) × m³ = N·m = J. These are the units of work.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Water shows anomalous behaviour
questions.ai_explanation: Between 0 °C and 4 °C, water contracts as it warms and expands as it cools. Its density is greatest at about 4 °C. This reversal of ordinary thermal expansion is its anomalous behaviour.
questions.explanation: Between 0 °C and 4 °C, water contracts as it warms and expands as it cools. Its density is greatest at about 4 °C. This reversal of ordinary thermal expansion is its anomalous behaviour.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which statement about a pure liquid in equilibrium with its vapour is NOT correct?

options.A: Boiling occurs when its saturated vapour pressure equals the external pressure.
options.B: Both its boiling point and its saturated vapour pressure at a fixed temperature depend on external pressure.
options.C: Its saturated vapour pressure rises as temperature increases.
options.D: Its saturated vapour pressure is independent of available volume while both liquid and vapour remain present.
options.E: Water can boil below 100 °C at high altitude.

questions.ai_explanation: At a fixed temperature, a pure liquid’s saturated vapour pressure is determined by the liquid and its temperature. External pressure sets the boiling temperature by the condition that vapour pressure equals external pressure.
questions.explanation: At a fixed temperature, a pure liquid’s saturated vapour pressure is determined by the liquid and its temperature. External pressure sets the boiling temperature by the condition that vapour pressure equals external pressure.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which phenomenon cannot be explained by a simple kinetic molecular model of matter alone?
questions.ai_explanation: Radiation transfers energy by electromagnetic waves and can cross a vacuum. A simple kinetic molecular model alone does not describe this mechanism; electromagnetic theory is also needed.
questions.explanation: Radiation transfers energy by electromagnetic waves and can cross a vacuum. A simple kinetic molecular model alone does not describe this mechanism; electromagnetic theory is also needed.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In order to find the depth of the sea. A ship sends out a sound wave and receives an echo after one second. If the velocity of sound in water is 1500m/s, what is the depth of the sea?
questions.ai_explanation: The echo time includes travel down to the seabed and back. Depth = vt/2 = 1500 × 1/2 = 750 m = 0.75 km.
questions.explanation: The echo time includes travel down to the seabed and back. Depth = vt/2 = 1500 × 1/2 = 750 m = 0.75 km.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: When a sound wave passes from air into water its

options.A: Speed and frequency increase but its wavelength remains the same.
options.B: Speed and wavelength increase but its frequency remains the same
options.D: Speed remains the same but its frequency and wavelength change.
options.E: Speed increases but its frequency and wavelength decrease.

questions.ai_explanation: Sound travels faster in water than in air. Its frequency stays fixed by the source as it crosses the boundary. Since λ = v/f, the wavelength increases with speed.
questions.explanation: Sound travels faster in water than in air. Its frequency stays fixed by the source as it crosses the boundary. Since λ = v/f, the wavelength increases with speed.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: If the fundamental frequency of a closed pipe organ on a day when the speed of sound is 340m s-1 is 170 Hz, then the length of the pipe is
questions.ai_explanation: For the fundamental of a pipe closed at one end, L = λ/4 = v/(4f). Thus L = 340/(4 × 170) = 0.50 m = 50 cm, neglecting end correction.
questions.explanation: For the fundamental of a pipe closed at one end, L = λ/4 = v/(4f). Thus L = 340/(4 × 170) = 0.50 m = 50 cm, neglecting end correction.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An object is placed 15cm in front of a concave mirror of radius 40cm. The image formed is

options.B: Real and 60cm in front of the mirror

questions.ai_explanation: The focal length is R/2 = 20 cm. With real distances positive, 1/v = 1/20 − 1/15 = −1/60. Thus the image is virtual, 60 cm behind the mirror; the object lies inside the focus.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A 45° triangular glass prism can be used as a reflector of light because

options.A: Refraction never takes place in such a prism
options.B: The angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence
options.C: The refractive index of glass is less than 1
options.E: The critical angle for glass is less than 45°

questions.ai_explanation: In a right-angled 45° glass prism, a ray entering normally at a short face reaches the long face at 45°. If the glass–air critical angle is smaller, total internal reflection occurs there.
questions.explanation: In a right-angled 45° glass prism, a ray entering normally at a short face reaches the long face at 45°. If the glass–air critical angle is smaller, total internal reflection occurs there.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Two rays from a point under a flat water surface lie in the same vertical plane, symmetrically about the vertical. Their angle in water is 60°. Find their angle in air to one decimal place. Take the refractive index of water as 4/3.
questions.ai_explanation: Each ray is 30° from the normal in water. Snell’s law gives sin r = (4/3)sin 30° = 2/3, so r = 41.81°. The emergent rays are separated by 2r = 83.6° to one decimal place.
questions.explanation: Each ray is 30° from the normal in water. Snell’s law gives sin r = (4/3)sin 30° = 2/3, so r = 41.81°. The emergent rays are separated by 2r = 83.6° to one decimal place.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following will convert a milliammeter to a voltmeter?

options.E: Parallel resistance equal to milliameter resistance.

questions.ai_explanation: A high resistance in series limits the current through the meter. The resulting combination measures a larger voltage because V = I(Rseries + Rmeter).
questions.explanation: A high resistance in series limits the current through the meter. The resulting combination measures a larger voltage because V = I(Rseries + Rmeter).

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An electric kettle connected to 240 V produces 6.0 × 10⁵ J of heat in 5 minutes. Find its resistance.
questions.ai_explanation: Five minutes is 300 s. Power = E/t = 600000/300 = 2000 W. Using P = V²/R gives R = 240²/2000 = 28.8 Ω.
questions.explanation: Five minutes is 300 s. Power = E/t = 600000/300 = 2000 W. Using P = V²/R gives R = 240²/2000 = 28.8 Ω.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: On which of the following does the operation of a moving coil ammeter depend? I Electromagnetic induction. II Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field. III Magnetic effect of an electric current.
questions.ai_explanation: A current-carrying coil experiences magnetic forces that produce a turning effect in the meter’s magnetic field. These are the magnetic effect of current and the force on a current-carrying conductor, so II and III apply.
questions.explanation: A current-carrying coil experiences magnetic forces that produce a turning effect in the meter’s magnetic field. These are the magnetic effect of current and the force on a current-carrying conductor, so II and III apply.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A 10 Ω resistor and a 5 Ω resistor are connected in parallel, with total current I entering their common junction. The 5 Ω resistor dissipates 40 W. What power does the 10 Ω resistor dissipate?
questions.ai_explanation: Parallel resistors have the same voltage across them. From the 5 Ω branch, V² = PR = 40 × 5 = 200 V². The power in the 10 Ω branch is therefore V²/10 = 200/10 = 20 W.
questions.explanation: Parallel resistors have the same voltage across them. From the 5 Ω branch, V² = PR = 40 × 5 = 200 V². The power in the 10 Ω branch is therefore V²/10 = 200/10 = 20 W.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following statements about electrolysis is NOT correct?

options.A: The substances in solution in the electrolyte become ionized.
options.B: Ions are electrically charged and are attracted towards electrodes when a potential difference is applied.
options.C: Ions may be discharged at the electrodes, forming bubbles or deposits.
options.D: The mass deposited depends upon the length of time for which current flows.
options.E: The mass of gas set free or metal deposited is proportional to the square of the current.

questions.ai_explanation: Faraday’s law gives deposited mass m = MIt/(nF). For the same material and duration, mass is proportional to current, not to its square.
questions.explanation: Faraday’s law gives deposited mass m = MIt/(nF). For the same material and duration, mass is proportional to current, not to its square.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which unit is equivalent to kg·m·s⁻¹?
questions.ai_explanation: One newton is kg·m·s⁻². Multiplying by one second gives N·s = kg·m·s⁻¹, the unit of momentum.
questions.explanation: One newton is kg·m·s⁻². Multiplying by one second gives N·s = kg·m·s⁻¹, the unit of momentum.

questions.question: Which of the following is a derived unit?
questions.ai_explanation: The newton is defined as kg·m·s⁻², combining base units to measure force. Kilogram, metre and kelvin are SI base units.
questions.explanation: The newton is defined as kg·m·s⁻², combining base units to measure force. Kilogram, metre and kelvin are SI base units.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Two objects, one with three times the mass of the other, are dropped together from the same height. Neglect air resistance. While falling above the ground, they have the same
questions.ai_explanation: Without air resistance, both objects accelerate at g and have the same velocity at each instant. Momentum, kinetic energy and gravitational potential energy also depend on mass, so these differ by a factor of three.
questions.explanation: Without air resistance, both objects accelerate at g and have the same velocity at each instant. Momentum, kinetic energy and gravitational potential energy also depend on mass, so these differ by a factor of three.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A uniform metre rule QR is horizontal, with Q at 0 cm and R at 100 cm. It balances on a knife edge 55 cm from R. A 10 g mass hangs at P, 10 cm from Q. What is the mass of the metre rule?
questions.ai_explanation: The pivot is at 100 − 55 = 45 cm from Q. The 10 g mass is 35 cm left of the pivot, while the uniform rule’s centre is 5 cm right of it. Balancing moments gives 10 × 35 = M × 5, so M = 70 g.
questions.explanation: The pivot is at 100 − 55 = 45 cm from Q. The 10 g mass is 35 cm left of the pivot, while the uniform rule’s centre is 5 cm right of it. Balancing moments gives 10 × 35 = M × 5, so M = 70 g.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Three forces F₁, F₂ and F₃ act at O in equilibrium. F₂ = 5.0 N points horizontally right. F₁ = 10.0 N points at 60° above F₂. What is the magnitude of F₃, to one decimal place?
questions.ai_explanation: F₃ must oppose the resultant of F₁ and F₂. The resultant’s squared magnitude is 10² + 5² + 2 × 10 × 5 cos 60° = 175 N². Hence |F₃| = √175 ≈ 13.2 N; its direction is opposite the resultant.
questions.explanation: F₃ must oppose the resultant of F₁ and F₂. The resultant’s squared magnitude is 10² + 5² + 2 × 10 × 5 cos 60° = 175 N². Hence |F₃| = √175 ≈ 13.2 N; its direction is opposite the resultant.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: When a box of mass 400g is given an initial speed of 5m s-1, it slides along a horizontal floor a distance of 3m before coming to rest. What is the coefficient of the kinetic friction between the box and the floor? (g = 10m s-2)
questions.ai_explanation: Work done against friction equals the initial kinetic energy: μmg × 3 = ½m × 5². Cancelling mass gives μ = 25/(2 × 10 × 3) = 5/12.
questions.explanation: Work done against friction equals the initial kinetic energy: μmg × 3 = ½m × 5². Cancelling mass gives μ = 25/(2 × 10 × 3) = 5/12.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A 1000 kg elevator descends with a downward acceleration of 1.0 m/s². If g = 10.0 m/s², what is the tension in its suspending cable?
questions.ai_explanation: Taking downward as positive, mg − T = ma. Therefore T = m(g − a) = 1000(10 − 1) = 9000 N. The downward acceleration makes tension less than weight.
questions.explanation: Taking downward as positive, mg − T = ma. Therefore T = m(g − a) = 1000(10 − 1) = 9000 N. The downward acceleration makes tension less than weight.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which mode of heat transfer does not require a material medium?
questions.ai_explanation: Thermal radiation travels as electromagnetic waves and can cross a vacuum. Conduction requires interacting matter, and convection requires moving fluid.
questions.explanation: Thermal radiation travels as electromagnetic waves and can cross a vacuum. Conduction requires interacting matter, and convection requires moving fluid.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Thermal expansion of solids can be a disadvantage in the
questions.ai_explanation: Thermal expansion changes the dimensions and moment of inertia of a watch’s balance wheel, affecting its oscillation period and timekeeping. Thermal compensation is needed to reduce this error.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The specific latent heat of fusion of lead is the amount of heat required to

options.A: Melt lead at its melting point
options.B: Heat unit mass of lead through 1 °C
options.C: Change unit mass of lead from solid to liquid at its melting point
options.D: Change the state of unit mass of lead at its boiling point

questions.question: Mercury is suitable as a barometric fluid because it

options.C: Is several times denser than water

questions.subject: physics

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A ray travelling in air strikes a glass surface at an incidence angle of 60°, measured from the normal. The reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular. Taking the refractive index of air as 1, what is the refractive index of the glass, to two decimal places?
questions.ai_explanation: The reflected angle equals the 60° incidence angle. Perpendicular reflected and refracted rays imply i + r =90°, so r =30°. Snell’s law gives n = sin 60°/sin 30° = √3 ≈1.73.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In which of the following arrangements is the wavelength in an increasing order?

options.A: Gamma rays, infra-red rays, X-rays, radiowaves.
options.B: Gamma rays, X-rays, infra-red rays, radiowaves.
options.C: Radiowaves, X-rays, gamma rays, infra-red rays.
options.D: Infra-red rays, radiowaves, X-rays, gamma rays.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: For light travelling from glass of refractive index 1.5 into air, what is the critical angle?
questions.ai_explanation: At the critical angle, the refracted ray in air is at 90°. Snell’s law gives 1.5 sin c = 1, so c = sin⁻¹(2/3). The incident ray must be travelling from glass toward air.
questions.explanation: At the critical angle, the refracted ray in air is at 90°. Snell’s law gives 1.5 sin c = 1, so c = sin⁻¹(2/3). The incident ray must be travelling from glass toward air.

questions.question: In the geometrical ray model of a pinhole camera, what happens to image sharpness when the hole is enlarged?

questions.subject: physics

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Radiation has wavelength 400 nm. Taking the speed of light in air as 3 × 10⁸ m/s, what is its frequency?

questions.explanation: Convert 400 nm to 400 × 10⁻⁹ m. Frequency f = c/λ = (3 × 10⁸)/(400 × 10⁻⁹) = 7.5 × 10¹⁴ Hz.

questions.question: The ideal mechanical advantage of a frictionless inclined plane depends on

options.C: The product of its length and height
options.D: The ratio of its length to its height

questions.explanation: Initial volume is 5³ = 125 cm³. To first order, volume expansivity is 3α, so V = 125[1 + 3(4 × 10⁻⁵)(120 − 20)] = 126.50 cm³.

questions.subject: physics

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An object 3.0cm high is placed 60.0cm from a converging lens whose focal length is 20.0cm. Calculate the size of the image formed.
questions.ai_explanation: The lens formula gives 1/v = 1/20 − 1/60 = 1/30, so v = 30 cm. Magnification magnitude is v/u = 30/60 = 0.5. Image height is 0.5 × 3.0 = 1.5 cm.
questions.explanation: The lens formula gives 1/v = 1/20 − 1/60 = 1/30, so v = 30 cm. Magnification magnitude is v/u = 30/60 = 0.5. Image height is 0.5 × 3.0 = 1.5 cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Four lenses are being considered for use as a microscope objective. Which of the following focal lengths is most suitable?
questions.ai_explanation: A microscope objective uses a converging lens with a short focal length. Positive 5 mm provides stronger convergence than positive 5 cm, making it the suitable choice here.
questions.explanation: A microscope objective uses a converging lens with a short focal length. Positive 5 mm provides stronger convergence than positive 5 cm, making it the suitable choice here.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: At a place with magnetic declination 10°E, a compass reads N40°E. What is the true geographic bearing?
questions.ai_explanation: Magnetic north is 10° east of true north. A compass direction 40° east of magnetic north is therefore 10° + 40° = 50° east of true north: N50°E.
questions.explanation: Magnetic north is 10° east of true north. A compass direction 40° east of magnetic north is therefore 10° + 40° = 50° east of true north: N50°E.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Capacitors of 6 μF and 8 μF are in series. What additional capacitor, connected in series with them, gives a total capacitance of 3 μF?
questions.ai_explanation: For series capacitors, reciprocals add: 1/3 = 1/6 + 1/8 + 1/C. Thus 1/C = 1/24 and the additional capacitance is 24 μF.
questions.explanation: For series capacitors, reciprocals add: 1/3 = 1/6 + 1/8 + 1/C. Thus 1/C = 1/24 and the additional capacitance is 24 μF.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An ideal transformer operating with a load has more turns on its secondary than its primary. It

options.A: Has a smaller secondary current than primary current
options.B: Has greater output power than input power
options.D: Increases the total energy output above its input

questions.ai_explanation: An ideal transformer with more secondary turns steps voltage up. Conservation of power gives VsIs = VpIp, so the secondary current is smaller than the primary current.
questions.explanation: An ideal transformer with more secondary turns steps voltage up. Conservation of power gives VsIs = VpIp, so the secondary current is smaller than the primary current.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The direction of the magnetic field at a point in the vicinity of a bar magnet is

options.A: Always towards the north pole of the magnet
options.B: Always away from the south pole of the magnet
options.C: Along the line joining the point to the neutral point
options.D: In the direction the north pole of a compass needle would point.

questions.ai_explanation: The direction of a magnetic field is defined as the direction in which the north-seeking pole of a small compass points at that location.
questions.explanation: The direction of a magnetic field is defined as the direction in which the north-seeking pole of a small compass points at that location.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: When two parallel wires carry currents in opposite directions, the force on either wire is

options.B: Zero, because the currents cancel each other
options.C: Twice as much as when the currents are in the same direction

questions.ai_explanation: Parallel conductors carrying currents in opposite directions repel. Each wire’s magnetic field exerts a force on the current in the other wire, directed away from it.
questions.explanation: Parallel conductors carrying currents in opposite directions repel. Each wire’s magnetic field exerts a force on the current in the other wire, directed away from it.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which statement is true of the ordinary single-photon photoelectric effect?

options.B: The maximum emitted-electron energy is independent of the surface work function
options.C: The maximum emitted-electron energy depends on the incident wavelength
options.D: At fixed wavelength, greater light intensity necessarily gives greater maximum emitted-electron energy

questions.ai_explanation: In the ordinary single-photon photoelectric effect, maximum kinetic energy is Kmax = hc/λ − φ. It depends on wavelength and work function. Increasing intensity at fixed wavelength chiefly increases the number emitted.
questions.explanation: In the ordinary single-photon photoelectric effect, maximum kinetic energy is Kmax = hc/λ − φ. It depends on wavelength and work function. Increasing intensity at fixed wavelength chiefly increases the number emitted.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Isotopes are nuclei which have

options.A: The same number of neutrons and electrons
options.B: Equal number of electrons and protons
options.C: The same atomic number but different number of neutrons
options.D: The same number of total particles.

questions.ai_explanation: Isotopes have the same atomic number, meaning the same number of protons, but different neutron numbers. Their mass numbers therefore differ.
questions.explanation: Isotopes have the same atomic number, meaning the same number of protons, but different neutron numbers. Their mass numbers therefore differ.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following is a set of vectors?

options.A: Force, mass and moment of force
options.B: Acceleration, velocity and moment of force

questions.ai_explanation: Acceleration and velocity have magnitude and direction. Moment of force, or torque, is also a vector with direction given by the right-hand rule. Mass, volume and density are scalars.
questions.explanation: Acceleration and velocity have magnitude and direction. Moment of force, or torque, is also a vector with direction given by the right-hand rule. Mass, volume and density are scalars.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which SI units are correctly matched? I. N for force. II. N·m⁻¹ for torque. III. W for power. IV. kg·m·s⁻² for momentum.
questions.ai_explanation: Force is measured in newtons and power in watts, so I and III are correct. Torque is measured in N·m, not N/m. Momentum is kg·m/s, not kg·m/s².
questions.explanation: Force is measured in newtons and power in watts, so I and III are correct. Torque is measured in N·m, not N/m. Momentum is kg·m/s, not kg·m/s².

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The magnitude of the resultant of two mutually perpendicular forces, F1 and F2 is 13N. If the magnitude of F1 is 5N, what is the magnitude of F2?
questions.ai_explanation: Perpendicular forces obey R² = F₁² + F₂². Therefore F₂ = √(13² − 5²) = √144 = 12 N.
questions.explanation: Perpendicular forces obey R² = F₁² + F₂². Therefore F₂ = √(13² − 5²) = √144 = 12 N.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A velocity–time graph contains points (5 s, 10 m/s) and (20 s, 20 m/s). Find the mean acceleration between them to two decimal places.
questions.ai_explanation: Mean acceleration is change in velocity divided by elapsed time: (20 − 10)/(20 − 5) = 10/15 = 0.67 m/s² to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: Mean acceleration is change in velocity divided by elapsed time: (20 − 10)/(20 − 5) = 10/15 = 0.67 m/s² to two decimal places.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Two perpendicular forces have resultant 100 N. One force makes 30° with the resultant. Find that force’s magnitude to one decimal place.
questions.ai_explanation: The force making 30° with the resultant is the adjacent component: F = R cos 30° = 100 × √3/2 = 86.6 N to one decimal place.
questions.explanation: The force making 30° with the resultant is the adjacent component: F = R cos 30° = 100 × √3/2 = 86.6 N to one decimal place.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following quantities are scalars? I Electrical potential II Torque III Momentum IV Kinetic energy
questions.ai_explanation: Electric potential and kinetic energy are scalars. Torque and momentum are vectors, so the scalar quantities are I and IV.
questions.explanation: Electric potential and kinetic energy are scalars. Torque and momentum are vectors, so the scalar quantities are I and IV.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A footballer applies an average force of 30.0 N to a stationary ball for 0.05 s. If the ball’s mass is 0.075 kg, what is its speed as it moves off?
questions.ai_explanation: Impulse equals change in momentum. Starting from rest, mv = Ft = 30.0 × 0.05 = 1.5 N·s. Hence v = 1.5/0.075 = 20.0 m/s.
questions.explanation: Impulse equals change in momentum. Starting from rest, mv = Ft = 30.0 × 0.05 = 1.5 N·s. Hence v = 1.5/0.075 = 20.0 m/s.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A 20-tooth gear drives a 60-tooth gear. If the smaller gear rotates at 120 rev/s, what is the angular speed of the larger gear?
questions.ai_explanation: Meshing gears pass the same number of teeth per second. Therefore 20 × 120 = 60 × n, giving the larger gear’s speed n = 40 rev/s.
questions.explanation: Meshing gears pass the same number of teeth per second. Therefore 20 × 120 = 60 × n, giving the larger gear’s speed n = 40 rev/s.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A 60 kg man climbs through a vertical height of 22 m with useful lifting power 0.25 kW. How long does the climb take? Use g = 10 m/s².
questions.ai_explanation: Useful energy for the climb is mgh = 60 × 10 × 22 = 13200 J. At 0.25 kW = 250 W, time = energy/power = 13200/250 = 52.8 s.
questions.explanation: Useful energy for the climb is mgh = 60 × 10 × 22 = 13200 J. At 0.25 kW = 250 W, time = energy/power = 13200/250 = 52.8 s.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The product PV where P is pressure and V is volume has the same unit as
questions.ai_explanation: Pressure × volume has units (N/m²) × m³ = N·m = J. A joule is the SI unit of energy.
questions.explanation: Pressure × volume has units (N/m²) × m³ = N·m = J. A joule is the SI unit of energy.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The amount of heat needed to raise the temperature of 10kg of copper by1K is its
questions.ai_explanation: Heat capacity refers to the whole body: C = Q/ΔT. The heat required for this 10 kg piece to rise by 1 K corresponds to its heat capacity. Specific heat capacity is per kilogram.
questions.explanation: Heat capacity refers to the whole body: C = Q/ΔT. The heat required for this 10 kg piece to rise by 1 K corresponds to its heat capacity. Specific heat capacity is per kilogram.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Heating one end of a metal rod causes lattice particles at the other end to vibrate more vigorously. Heat has been transferred through the rod by
questions.ai_explanation: Conduction transfers thermal energy through the rod without bulk motion of the metal. In metals, mobile electrons and lattice vibrations both contribute to this transfer.
questions.explanation: Conduction transfers thermal energy through the rod without bulk motion of the metal. In metals, mobile electrons and lattice vibrations both contribute to this transfer.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following media allow the transmission of sound waves through them? I Air II Liquids III Solids
questions.ai_explanation: Sound is a mechanical disturbance that can propagate through gases, liquids and solids. All three provide matter whose particles can pass the disturbance onward.
questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical disturbance that can propagate through gases, liquids and solids. All three provide matter whose particles can pass the disturbance onward.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which behaviours can both mechanical and electromagnetic waves exhibit under suitable conditions? I. Diffraction. II. Refraction. III. Interference.
questions.ai_explanation: Mechanical and electromagnetic waves can diffract around openings, refract when their propagation speed changes, and interfere when they overlap. All three are characteristic wave behaviours.
questions.explanation: Mechanical and electromagnetic waves can diffract around openings, refract when their propagation speed changes, and interfere when they overlap. All three are characteristic wave behaviours.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In the usual nondispersive ideal-gas model for air of fixed composition, which factor independently affects sound speed? I. Temperature. II. Pressure at fixed temperature. III. Frequency.
questions.ai_explanation: For air treated as an ideal gas, sound speed is √(γRT/M). At fixed composition it depends on temperature. Pressure has no independent effect at fixed temperature, and frequency does not enter this model.
questions.explanation: For air treated as an ideal gas, sound speed is √(γRT/M). At fixed composition it depends on temperature. Pressure has no independent effect at fixed temperature, and frequency does not enter this model.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The speed of sound in air at sea-level is 340m s-1 while that of light is 300,000km s-1. How far (to the nearest metre) from the center of thunderstorm is an observer who hears a thunder 2s after a lightning flash?
questions.ai_explanation: The delay is d/340 − d/(3 × 10⁸) = 2 s. Solving gives d ≈ 680.0008 m, which rounds to 680 m. Neglecting the tiny light travel time gives the same metre-rounded result.
questions.explanation: The delay is d/340 − d/(3 × 10⁸) = 2 s. Solving gives d ≈ 680.0008 m, which rounds to 680 m. Neglecting the tiny light travel time gives the same metre-rounded result.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Two uniform strings of equal length and equal tension sound their fundamental notes in frequency ratio 4:1. What is their corresponding mass ratio?
questions.ai_explanation: For equal length and tension in the same vibration mode, f is proportional to 1/√m. Thus f₁/f₂ = 4 implies m₁/m₂ = (1/4)² = 1/16.
questions.explanation: For equal length and tension in the same vibration mode, f is proportional to 1/√m. Thus f₁/f₂ = 4 implies m₁/m₂ = (1/4)² = 1/16.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An object is placed 10 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. What is the position and nature of the image?

options.B: 6 cm in front of the mirror, real
options.D: 30 cm in front of the mirror, real

questions.ai_explanation: With real object distance positive, 1/v = 1/15 − 1/10 = −1/30. The image is therefore virtual and lies 30 cm behind the mirror. The object is inside the focal length.
questions.explanation: With real object distance positive, 1/v = 1/15 − 1/10 = −1/30. The image is therefore virtual and lies 30 cm behind the mirror. The object is inside the focal length.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: When white light is dispersed by a spectrometer, the component having the shortest wavelength is
questions.ai_explanation: Violet is at the short-wavelength end of the visible spectrum. Green, orange and red all have longer wavelengths than violet.
questions.explanation: Violet is at the short-wavelength end of the visible spectrum. Green, orange and red all have longer wavelengths than violet.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following statements is TRUE of ultra- violet, visible and infra-red rays?

options.A: They are all electromagnetic waves with the same wavelength
options.B: Ultraviolet rays have shorter wavelengths than infrared rays and can produce fluorescence
options.C: Infrared rays have shorter wavelengths than visible light and produce a sensation of heat
options.D: Wavelengths increase in the order visible, ultraviolet, infrared

questions.ai_explanation: Ultraviolet has shorter wavelengths than visible light and infrared. It can excite fluorescent materials, which then emit light, often at visible wavelengths.
questions.explanation: Ultraviolet has shorter wavelengths than visible light and infrared. It can excite fluorescent materials, which then emit light, often at visible wavelengths.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Connecting a resistance R across a cell reduces its terminal voltage to two-thirds of its open-circuit emf. What is the cell’s internal resistance?
questions.ai_explanation: With external resistance R and internal resistance r, terminal voltage is V = ER/(R + r). Setting V/E = 2/3 gives 3R = 2(R + r), hence r = R/2.
questions.explanation: With external resistance R and internal resistance r, terminal voltage is V = ER/(R + r). Setting V/E = 2/3 gives 3R = 2(R + r), hence r = R/2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: At the given voltage and power ratings, which instrument draws the highest current?
questions.ai_explanation: Using I = P/V: iron = 1000/250 = 4 A; television = 110/220 = 0.5 A; torch = 30/6 = 5 A; heater = 500/110 ≈ 4.55 A. The torch draws the highest current.
questions.explanation: Using I = P/V: iron = 1000/250 = 4 A; television = 110/220 = 0.5 A; torch = 30/6 = 5 A; heater = 500/110 ≈ 4.55 A. The torch draws the highest current.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which instruments can directly measure ordinary alternating current without an added rectifier? I. Permanent-magnet moving-coil ammeter. II. Moving-iron ammeter. III. Hot-wire ammeter.
questions.ai_explanation: Moving-iron meters respond to magnetization irrespective of current direction. Hot-wire meters respond to I²R heating. Both can measure AC. An unrectified permanent-magnet moving-coil meter averages opposing torques over an AC cycle.
questions.explanation: Moving-iron meters respond to magnetization irrespective of current direction. Hot-wire meters respond to I²R heating. Both can measure AC. An unrectified permanent-magnet moving-coil meter averages opposing torques over an AC cycle.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The principle of operation of an induction coil is based on
questions.ai_explanation: An induction coil uses a changing current to change magnetic flux through another winding. Faraday’s law relates that changing flux to the induced emf.
questions.explanation: An induction coil uses a changing current to change magnetic flux through another winding. Faraday’s law relates that changing flux to the induced emf.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which notation represents a neutral atom X with 22 electrons and 43 neutrons?
questions.ai_explanation: For a neutral atom, 22 electrons mean 22 protons, so atomic number Z = 22. Mass number A = protons + neutrons = 22 + 43 = 65. The notation is ⁶⁵₂₂X.
questions.explanation: For a neutral atom, 22 electrons mean 22 protons, so atomic number Z = 22. Mass number A = protons + neutrons = 22 + 43 = 65. The notation is ⁶⁵₂₂X.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following devices are used to measure pressure? I Aneroid barometer II Hydrometer III Hygrometer IV Manometer.
questions.ai_explanation: An aneroid barometer measures atmospheric pressure and a manometer measures pressure or pressure difference. A hydrometer measures liquid density, while a hygrometer measures humidity.
questions.explanation: An aneroid barometer measures atmospheric pressure and a manometer measures pressure or pressure difference. A hydrometer measures liquid density, while a hygrometer measures humidity.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An electric heater melts 1.5 kg of ice initially at 0 °C. It draws 20 A from a 12 V battery. Assuming all its heat melts the ice, find the time taken. Use specific latent heat of fusion 336 × 10³ J/kg.
questions.ai_explanation: Heat needed is mL = 1.5 × 336000 = 504000 J. Heater power is VI = 12 × 20 = 240 W. Time = 504000/240 = 2100 s = 35.0 min.
questions.explanation: Heat needed is mL = 1.5 × 336000 = 504000 J. Heater power is VI = 12 × 20 = 240 W. Time = 504000/240 = 2100 s = 35.0 min.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In the kinetic theory of an ideal gas, absolute temperature is a

options.A: Form of energy proportional to the total kinetic energy of its molecules
options.B: Form of energy proportional to the average kinetic energy of its molecules
options.C: Physical property proportional to the total kinetic energy of its molecules
options.D: Physical property proportional to the average translational kinetic energy of its molecules

questions.ai_explanation: Absolute temperature is a physical property, not a quantity of energy. For an ideal gas, the mean translational kinetic energy per molecule is 3kT/2, so it is proportional to kelvin temperature.
questions.explanation: Absolute temperature is a physical property, not a quantity of energy. For an ideal gas, the mean translational kinetic energy per molecule is 3kT/2, so it is proportional to kelvin temperature.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In a sound wave in air, the adjacent rarefactions and compressions are separated by a distance of 17cm. If the velocity of the sound wave is 340ms-1, determine the frequency.
questions.ai_explanation: A compression and the adjacent rarefaction are half a wavelength apart. Thus λ = 2 × 17 cm = 0.34 m. Frequency f = v/λ = 340/0.34 = 1000 Hz.
questions.explanation: A compression and the adjacent rarefaction are half a wavelength apart. Thus λ = 2 × 17 cm = 0.34 m. Frequency f = v/λ = 340/0.34 = 1000 Hz.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Light of free-space wavelength 5000 × 10⁻⁸ cm enters glass of refractive index 1.5. Find its wavelength in glass, rounding the coefficient of 10⁻⁸ cm to the nearest integer.
questions.ai_explanation: Frequency stays unchanged on entering glass, while speed becomes c/n. Therefore wavelength becomes λ/n = (5000/1.5) × 10⁻⁸ cm ≈ 3333 × 10⁻⁸ cm.
questions.explanation: Frequency stays unchanged on entering glass, while speed becomes c/n. Therefore wavelength becomes λ/n = (5000/1.5) × 10⁻⁸ cm ≈ 3333 × 10⁻⁸ cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The magnification of the image of an object placed in front of a convex mirror is 1/3. If the radius of curvature of the mirror is 24cm, what is the distance between the object and its image?
questions.ai_explanation: For a convex mirror, f = −12 cm and v = −u/3. The mirror equation gives −1/12 = 1/u − 3/u = −2/u, so u = 24 cm and v = −8 cm. Their separation is 24 + 8 = 32 cm.
questions.explanation: For a convex mirror, f = −12 cm and v = −u/3. The mirror equation gives −1/12 = 1/u − 3/u = −2/u, so u = 24 cm and v = −8 cm. Their separation is 24 + 8 = 32 cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In a common three-mirror kaleidoscope with an equilateral triangular cross-section, adjacent plane mirrors are placed
questions.ai_explanation: A common three-mirror kaleidoscope uses mirrors forming an equilateral triangular tube. Adjacent mirrors meet at 60°, creating repeated symmetric images by reflection.
questions.explanation: A common three-mirror kaleidoscope uses mirrors forming an equilateral triangular tube. Adjacent mirrors meet at 60°, creating repeated symmetric images by reflection.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Under white light, an ideal yellow card is viewed through an ideal blue filter. What colour does the card appear?
questions.ai_explanation: In the ideal colour model, a yellow card reflects red and green light. A blue filter transmits blue and blocks red and green, leaving essentially no light from the card, so it appears black.
questions.explanation: In the ideal colour model, a yellow card reflects red and green light. A blue filter transmits blue and blocks red and green, leaving essentially no light from the card, so it appears black.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Dispersion of light by a glass prism is due to the

options.A: Different hidden colours of the glass
options.B: Different speeds of the various colours in glass

questions.ai_explanation: Glass has a refractive index that depends on wavelength. Different colours therefore travel at different speeds in it and refract by different amounts, separating the white light.
questions.explanation: Glass has a refractive index that depends on wavelength. Different colours therefore travel at different speeds in it and refract by different amounts, separating the white light.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following pairs is NOT part of the electromagnetic spectrum? I Radio waves II Beta rays III Gamma rays IV Alpha rays
questions.ai_explanation: Alpha radiation consists of helium nuclei and beta radiation of electrons or positrons. They are particles with mass. Radio waves and gamma rays are electromagnetic radiation.
questions.explanation: Alpha radiation consists of helium nuclei and beta radiation of electrons or positrons. They are particles with mass. Radio waves and gamma rays are electromagnetic radiation.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Two insulated conducting spheres of different sizes carry opposite charges. They are connected by a metal wire. Charge flows until both spheres

options.A: Carry the same magnitude and sign of charge.

questions.ai_explanation: Charges redistribute through the connecting conductor until there is no potential difference between the spheres. At electrostatic equilibrium the connected conductor is equipotential.
questions.explanation: Charges redistribute through the connecting conductor until there is no potential difference between the spheres. At electrostatic equilibrium the connected conductor is equipotential.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A uniform wire 5 m long has cross-sectional area 0.2 × 10⁻⁶ m² and resistance 0.425 Ω. Find its resistivity.
questions.ai_explanation: For a uniform wire R = ρL/A. Thus ρ = RA/L = 0.425 × (0.2 × 10⁻⁶)/5 = 1.70 × 10⁻⁸ Ω·m.
questions.explanation: For a uniform wire R = ρL/A. Thus ρ = RA/L = 0.425 × (0.2 × 10⁻⁶)/5 = 1.70 × 10⁻⁸ Ω·m.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Resistors of 250 Ω, 500 Ω and 1 kΩ are connected in series across a 6 V battery. Find the voltage across the 250 Ω resistor to two decimal places.
questions.ai_explanation: Series resistance is 250 + 500 + 1000 = 1750 Ω. The 250 Ω resistor gets the fraction 250/1750 of the voltage: 6 × 250/1750 = 0.86 V to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: Series resistance is 250 + 500 + 1000 = 1750 Ω. The 250 Ω resistor gets the fraction 250/1750 of the voltage: 6 × 250/1750 = 0.86 V to two decimal places.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An ammeter of resistance 0.1 Ω has full-scale current 50 mA. A 0.0111 Ω shunt is connected across it. Find the new full-scale total current to the nearest milliampere.
questions.ai_explanation: At full scale, the meter voltage is 0.050 × 0.1 = 0.005 V. The shunt carries 0.005/0.0111 ≈ 0.45045 A. Adding the meter’s 0.050 A gives 0.50045 A, or 500 mA to the nearest milliampere.
questions.explanation: At full scale, the meter voltage is 0.050 × 0.1 = 0.005 V. The shunt carries 0.005/0.0111 ≈ 0.45045 A. Adding the meter’s 0.050 A gives 0.50045 A, or 500 mA to the nearest milliampere.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The electrochemical equivalent of silver is 0.0012 g/C. What steady current deposits 36.0 g in 5.0 minutes?
questions.ai_explanation: Deposited mass is m = ZIt. With time 5 × 60 = 300 s, I = 36/(0.0012 × 300) = 100 A.
questions.explanation: Deposited mass is m = ZIt. With time 5 × 60 = 300 s, I = 36/(0.0012 × 300) = 100 A.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: For a fixed metal surface in the ordinary single-photon photoelectric effect, the maximum kinetic energy of an emitted electron depends on the
questions.ai_explanation: For a fixed metal in the ordinary photoelectric effect, Kmax = hc/λ − φ. The wavelength sets photon energy and therefore the maximum emitted-electron energy above the work function.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following is a fundamental unit?
questions.ai_explanation: The second is the SI base unit of time. Newton, watt and joule are derived units built from kilogram, metre and second.
questions.explanation: The second is the SI base unit of time. Newton, watt and joule are derived units built from kilogram, metre and second.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An engine supplies useful mechanical power P to keep a vehicle moving at constant speed v. What driving force does it provide?
questions.ai_explanation: Mechanical power for a force along the direction of motion is P = Fv. Dividing by speed gives the engine’s driving force F = P/v.
questions.explanation: Mechanical power for a force along the direction of motion is P = Fv. Dividing by speed gives the engine’s driving force F = P/v.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: What liquid-column height supports atmospheric pressure 102000 N/m² if liquid density is 2600 kg/m³ and g = 10 m/s²? Give the answer to two decimal places.
questions.ai_explanation: Hydrostatic pressure is p = ρgh. Thus h = 102000/(2600 × 10) = 3.923… m, or 3.92 m to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: Hydrostatic pressure is p = ρgh. Thus h = 102000/(2600 × 10) = 3.923… m, or 3.92 m to two decimal places.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A platinum wire has resistance 0.75 Ω at 0 °C and 1.05 Ω at 100 °C. Assuming linear variation, find its temperature when resistance is 0.90 Ω.
questions.ai_explanation: The 0–100 °C resistance change is 1.05 − 0.75 = 0.30 Ω. The measured rise is 0.90 − 0.75 = 0.15 Ω, half the interval. Temperature is therefore 50.0 °C.
questions.explanation: The 0–100 °C resistance change is 1.05 − 0.75 = 0.30 Ω. The measured rise is 0.90 − 0.75 = 0.15 Ω, half the interval. Temperature is therefore 50.0 °C.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A fixed amount of gas is cooled at constant volume without condensation. Its pressure decreases because its molecules

options.A: Collide less frequently with the walls of the container.
options.B: Have the same average kinetic energy

questions.ai_explanation: Cooling lowers the molecules’ average kinetic energy and speed. At fixed volume they strike the walls less often and with less momentum change per collision, reducing the gas pressure.
questions.explanation: Cooling lowers the molecules’ average kinetic energy and speed. At fixed volume they strike the walls less often and with less momentum change per collision, reducing the gas pressure.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A 1 kg copper block at 100 °C is placed on ice at 0 °C. Neglect heat loss. Find the mass melted to the nearest gram, using copper’s specific heat capacity 400 J/(kg·K) and ice’s latent heat of fusion 333 × 10³ J/kg.
questions.ai_explanation: The copper loses Q = mcΔT = 1 × 400 × 100 = 40000 J. This melts ice of mass Q/L = 40000/333000 = 0.12012… kg, or 120 g to the nearest gram.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In ordinary heat-transfer experiments, which statements are correct? I. Land and sea breezes are natural convection currents. II. questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Geometrical shadows and eclipses result primarily from the

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An object 3 cm high is placed vertically 10 cm in front of a concave mirror. Its image is 40 cm from the mirror. Find the magnitude of the image height.
questions.ai_explanation: The magnitude of magnification is image distance divided by object distance: 40/10 = 4. Therefore the image height has magnitude 4 × 3 = 12 cm.
questions.explanation: The magnitude of magnification is image distance divided by object distance: 40/10 = 4. Therefore the image height has magnitude 4 × 3 = 12 cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: What must be the distance between an object and a converging lens of focal length 20cm to produce an erect image two times the object height?
questions.ai_explanation: An erect image from a converging lens is virtual: v = −2u. Substituting in 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/20 = 1/(2u). Hence u = 10 cm, inside the focal length.
questions.explanation: An erect image from a converging lens is virtual: v = −2u. Substituting in 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/20 = 1/(2u). Hence u = 10 cm, inside the focal length.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In an uncorrected short-sighted eye, light rays from a point on a very distant object are focused

questions.question: Under white illumination, which primary colour does an ideal magenta surface absorb?

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In a resonance tube closed at one end, the first resonant air-column length is 20 cm for a 480 Hz tuning fork. Neglect end correction and find the speed of sound.

questions.question: An organ pipe closed at one end is 80 cm long. Neglect end correction. Find its fundamental frequency to the nearest hertz if sound speed is 340 m/s.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Three identical cells, each of emf 1.5 V and internal resistance 1.0 Ω, are connected in parallel with matching polarity across a 2.67 Ω load. Find the load current to two decimal places.
questions.ai_explanation: Identical cells in parallel retain emf 1.5 V and have internal resistance 1/3 Ω. The load current is 1.5/(2.67 + 1/3) = 0.4994… A, or 0.50 A to two decimal places.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: In a uniform metre bridge, a 2.0 Ω standard resistor occupies the gap beside the 0 cm end. The balance point is 55.0 cm from that end. Find the resistance in the other gap to two decimal places.
questions.ai_explanation: For a uniform metre bridge, resistance ratio equals wire-length ratio at balance. With 2.0 Ω beside the 0 cm end, 2.0/R = 55/45. Thus R = 2.0 × 45/55 = 1.64 Ω to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: For a uniform metre bridge, resistance ratio equals wire-length ratio at balance. With 2.0 Ω beside the 0 cm end, 2.0/R = 55/45. Thus R = 2.0 × 45/55 = 1.64 Ω to two decimal places.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The energy supplied by an electrical source per unit positive charge for a complete circuit is its

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following is an essential physical property of the wires used for making fuses?

questions.explanation: A fuse element must melt when excessive current heats it sufficiently. Melting opens the circuit and stops the sustained overcurrent. A suitably low melting point supports this protective action.

questions.question: For the same transmitted power, using a higher voltage reduces energy lost in the transmission wires through
questions.ai_explanation: For the same transmitted power, increasing voltage reduces current because P = VI. Heating loss in the wires is I²R, so lowering current reduces heat dissipation.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A galvanometer with full-scale current 10 mA and coil resistance 30 Ω is converted to a 10 A ammeter. Which approximate resistor and connection are required?

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: What precaution should a manufacturer take to ensure that energy loss in a transformer is minimized?

options.A: Make the windings from high-resistance wire
options.B: Make the magnetic core from thin, electrically insulated metal sheets

options.D: Minimize flux linking the primary and secondary coils

questions.question: A photoemissive photocell works on the principle of

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An object moves with uniform speed round a circle. Its acceleration has

questions.question: The spiral spring of a spring balance is 25.0cm long when 5N hangs on it and 30.0cm long, when the weight is 10N. What is the length of the spring if the weight is 3N assuming Hooke’s Law is obeyed?

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A stone gives an apparent mass reading of 15.0 g when fully immersed in water and 10.0 g when fully immersed in a liquid of relative density 2.0. Neglect air buoyancy. Find its mass in air.
questions.ai_explanation: Let b be the mass-equivalent buoyancy in water and m the true mass. Then m − b = 15 g and m − 2b = 10 g. Subtracting gives b = 5 g, so m = 20 g.
questions.explanation: Let b be the mass-equivalent buoyancy in water and m the true mass. Then m − b = 15 g and m − 2b = 10 g. Subtracting gives b = 5 g, so m = 20 g.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: At normal atmospheric pressure, how much more heat is released by 4 kg of steam at 100 °C than by 4 kg of water at 100 °C when each ends as water at 80 °C? Use latent heat 2260000 J/kg and water specific heat 4200 J/(kg·K).

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which statement is true of light waves and sound waves in air?

options.D: Their speeds in air are equal

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The image in pin-hole camera is

options.A: Erect and formed by refraction through a lens
options.C: Erect and gets sharper as the hole becomes larger
options.D: Inverted and formed by the light from each point traveling in a straight line.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A plane mirror is rotated through a small angle Q in the plane of incidence while the incident ray remains fixed. Through what angle does the reflected ray rotate?
questions.ai_explanation: With the incident ray fixed, rotating the mirror also rotates its normal by Q. The equal-angle reflection law makes the reflected direction change by twice that angle, or 2Q.

options.B: Pass through the center of curvature after refraction
options.C: Emerge parallel to the principal axis
options.D: Pass through the principal focus after refraction.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the image of an object, 4cm from a diverging lens of focal length –12cm?

options.B: The image is real, 6cm behind the lens

questions.question: Two tuning forks of frequencies 256Hz and 260 Hz are sounded close to each other. What is the frequency of the beats produced?

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following statements is CORRECT about the earth’s magnetic field?

options.A: The angle of dip is the angle which a free suspended magnet makes with the vertical
options.B: The angle of declination is the angle between the magnetic meridian and the geographic meridian
options.C: The angle of declination is the angle which a magnetic compass makes with the magnetic meridian.
options.D: The angle of inclination is the difference between the angle of dip and the angle of declination.

questions.ai_explanation: Magnetic declination is the horizontal angle between geographic north and magnetic north. Dip, or inclination, is instead the angle of the magnetic field relative to the horizontal.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The function of the system of granulated carbon mixed with manganese (IV) oxide in a Leclanche cell is to

options.B: Prevent local action in the cell
options.D: Make the cell black and hence a good radiator

questions.question: A resistive device dissipates 1500 W and has resistance 375 Ω. What current does it draw?

questions.explanation: For a resistive device, P = I²R. Hence I = √(P/R) = √(1500/375) = √4 = 2.00 A.

questions.subject: physics

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The speed of light in air is 3.0 ×10⁸ m/s. Find its speed in glass of refractive index 1.50 relative to air.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The angle between the direction of the earth’s magnetic field and the horizontal is called the

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which change does not alter the equilibrium emf of a primary cell, with chemistry and other conditions otherwise unchanged?

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A 5 V battery is connected across an initially uncharged 2.0 μF capacitor. After a long time, what is the magnitude of charge on either plate?

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: For resistive devices with the same proportional protection margin, which has the smallest operating current and therefore needs the lowest fuse current rating?

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: For steady current I through a constant resistance R for time t, the heat produced is

options.A: Inversely proportional to the current and the resistance
options.B: Directly proportional to the current, resistance and the time.
options.C: Inversely proportional to the square of the resistance, current and the time.
options.D: Directly proportional to the square of the current, the resistance and the time.

questions.explanation: Joule heating is H =I²Rt for a steady current through a constant resistance. Heat is proportional to current squared, resistance and elapsed time.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A galvanometer has resistance 10 Ω and full-scale current 0.05 A. What added resistance converts it into a 100 V voltmeter, and how is it connected?
questions.ai_explanation: The total required resistance is V/I =100/0.05 =2000 Ω. Subtracting the galvanometer’s 10 Ω gives R =1990 Ω. It is connected in series to limit the current through the meter.
questions.explanation: The total required resistance is V/I =100/0.05 =2000 Ω. Subtracting the galvanometer’s 10 Ω gives R =1990 Ω. It is connected in series to limit the current through the meter.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The units of impedance, RMS voltage and resonance frequency are respectively
questions.ai_explanation: Impedance is voltage divided by current, so its unit is the ohm. RMS voltage is measured in volts, and resonance frequency in hertz, or cycles per second.
questions.explanation: Impedance is voltage divided by current, so its unit is the ohm. RMS voltage is measured in volts, and resonance frequency in hertz, or cycles per second.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: For a sinusoidal alternating current with peak I₀, which relation gives its RMS current Iᵣₘₛ?
questions.ai_explanation: For sinusoidal current, the mean of sin² over a cycle is 1/2. Thus the mean square current is I₀²/2, and its square root is Iᵣₘₛ =I₀/√2.
questions.explanation: For sinusoidal current, the mean of sin² over a cycle is 1/2. Thus the mean square current is I₀²/2, and its square root is Iᵣₘₛ =I₀/√2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following quantities has the same unit as the watt?
questions.ai_explanation: A watt is a joule per second. Force multiplied by velocity has units N·m/s =J/s =W, so it has the unit of power.
questions.explanation: A watt is a joule per second. Force multiplied by velocity has units N·m/s =J/s =W, so it has the unit of power.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Two forces of 7 N and 3 N act at right angles. If θ is the angle between the resultant and the 7 N force, which relation holds?
questions.ai_explanation: The resultant has components 7 N along the larger force and 3 N perpendicular to it. Therefore tan θ =opposite/adjacent =3/7.
questions.explanation: The resultant has components 7 N along the larger force and 3 N perpendicular to it. Therefore tan θ =opposite/adjacent =3/7.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An object is projected at 80 m/s,30° above horizontal. Neglect air resistance and use g =10 m/s². Find its maximum height above the launch point.
questions.ai_explanation: The initial upward velocity is 80 sin 30° =40 m/s. At maximum height the vertical velocity is zero, so h =40²/(2 ×10) =80 m.
questions.explanation: The initial upward velocity is 80 sin 30° =40 m/s. At maximum height the vertical velocity is zero, so h =40²/(2 ×10) =80 m.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An aeroplane lands at 180 km/h and slows uniformly to rest in 30 s. What distance does it cover before stopping?
questions.ai_explanation: The landing speed is 180/3.6 =50 m/s. Uniform deceleration gives average speed(50 +0)/2 =25 m/s, so distance is 25 ×30 =750 m.
questions.explanation: The landing speed is 180/3.6 =50 m/s. Uniform deceleration gives average speed(50 +0)/2 =25 m/s, so distance is 25 ×30 =750 m.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A particle moves in a fixed horizontal circle at constant angular velocity. Which statement is true?

options.A: Kinetic energy is constant but linear momentum varies
options.B: Linear momentum is constant but kinetic energy varies
options.C: Kinetic energy and linear momentum are both constant
options.D: Speed and linear velocity are both constant

questions.ai_explanation: At constant angular velocity on a fixed circle, speed is constant, so kinetic energy stays constant. The direction of velocity changes continuously, making linear momentum change direction.
questions.explanation: At constant angular velocity on a fixed circle, speed is constant, so kinetic energy stays constant. The direction of velocity changes continuously, making linear momentum change direction.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Starting with water stored at height, which sequence describes the main energy conversions when a hydroelectric station powers a lamp?
questions.ai_explanation: Water stored above a turbine has gravitational potential energy. Flowing water turns the turbine, which drives a generator. Electrical energy from the generator is then converted to light by a lamp.
questions.explanation: Water stored above a turbine has gravitational potential energy. Flowing water turns the turbine, which drives a generator. Electrical energy from the generator is then converted to light by a lamp.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: An object of mass 400 g and density 600 kg/m³ hangs at rest from a string with half its volume immersed in paraffin of density 900 kg/m³. Find the string tension. Use g =10 m/s².
questions.ai_explanation: The object weighs 0.4 ×10 =4 N. Half its volume displaces paraffin of mass 0.5 ×0.4 ×900/600 =0.3 kg, giving 3 N upthrust. The string tension is 4 −3 =1 N.
questions.explanation: The object weighs 0.4 ×10 =4 N. Half its volume displaces paraffin of mass 0.5 ×0.4 ×900/600 =0.3 kg, giving 3 N upthrust. The string tension is 4 −3 =1 N.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: With its reference-junction temperature fixed, a thermocouple measures temperature through changes in its
questions.ai_explanation: With the reference junction held at a known temperature, a thermocouple’s emf changes with the measuring-junction temperature. Calibration relates that voltage to temperature.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A fixed mass of ideal gas has its volume halved and absolute temperature doubled. What happens to its pressure?
questions.ai_explanation: For a fixed amount of ideal gas, P is proportional toT/V. Doubling absolute temperature while halving volume multiplies pressure by 2/(1/2) =4.
questions.explanation: For a fixed amount of ideal gas, P is proportional toT/V. Doubling absolute temperature while halving volume multiplies pressure by 2/(1/2) =4.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Mix 200 g of water at 90 °C with 100 g of water at 30 °C. Neglect heat loss and the container’s heat capacity. What is the final temperature?
questions.ai_explanation: Ignoring heat loss, heat lost by hot water equals heat gained by cool water:200(90 −T) =100(T −30). Solving gives 300 T =21000, so T =70 °C.
questions.explanation: Ignoring heat loss, heat lost by hot water equals heat gained by cool water:200(90 −T) =100(T −30). Solving gives 300 T =21000, so T =70 °C.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A solid melts at 80 °C. At that temperature,10⁵ J melts 10 g of the solid. Find its specific latent heat of fusion.
questions.ai_explanation: At the melting point, heat goes into the phase change. The mass is 10 g =0.010 kg, so specific latent heat is Q/m =10⁵/0.010 =1.00 ×10⁷ J/kg.
questions.explanation: At the melting point, heat goes into the phase change. The mass is 10 g =0.010 kg, so specific latent heat is Q/m =10⁵/0.010 =1.00 ×10⁷ J/kg.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A stationary wave has wavelength 60 cm. Find the distance between consecutive antinodes.
questions.ai_explanation: Consecutive antinodes of a stationary wave are half a wavelength apart. Their separation is therefore 60/2 =30 cm.
questions.explanation: Consecutive antinodes of a stationary wave are half a wavelength apart. Their separation is therefore 60/2 =30 cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following waves can propagate through a vacuum?
questions.ai_explanation: Infrared radiation is electromagnetic and can travel through vacuum. Sound, ultrasound and other acoustic waves need a material medium for their pressure disturbances.
questions.explanation: Infrared radiation is electromagnetic and can travel through vacuum. Sound, ultrasound and other acoustic waves need a material medium for their pressure disturbances.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A radar pulse returns to its transmitting antenna 4 ×10⁻³ s after reflection from an aircraft. How far away is the aircraft? Use c =3 ×10⁸ m/s.
questions.ai_explanation: The measured time includes the outward and return journeys. One-way distance is ct/2 =(3 ×10⁸)(4 ×10⁻³)/2 =6 ×10⁵ m =6 ×10² km.
questions.explanation: The measured time includes the outward and return journeys. One-way distance is ct/2 =(3 ×10⁸)(4 ×10⁻³)/2 =6 ×10⁵ m =6 ×10² km.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A concave mirror of radius r forms a real image. Let u and v be the positive object and image distances. Which expression gives the magnitude of linear magnification?
questions.ai_explanation: For a real image, magnification magnitude is v/u. Since 1/u +1/v =2/r, multiplying byv gives v/u +1 =2 v/r. Therefore magnification magnitude is 2 v/r −1.
questions.explanation: For a real image, magnification magnitude is v/u. Since 1/u +1/v =2/r, multiplying byv gives v/u +1 =2 v/r. Therefore magnification magnitude is 2 v/r −1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: A thin camera lens has focal length 20 cm. An object is 100 cm from the lens. What lens-to-film distance gives a sharp image?
questions.ai_explanation: Using 1/f =1/u +1/v gives 1/v =1/20 −1/100 =1/25. The film must therefore be 25 cm from the lens to receive the sharp real image.
questions.explanation: Using 1/f =1/u +1/v gives 1/v =1/20 −1/100 =1/25. The film must therefore be 25 cm from the lens to receive the sharp real image.

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: The property of the eye known as its power of accommodation is controlled by the

questions.subject: physics
questions.question: Which of the following correctly explain(s) why soft iron is preferred to steel in electromagnets? I Soft iron is more readily magnetized than steel. II Soft iron is more readily demagnetized than steel. III Soft iron retains magnetism more than steel.
questions.ai_explanation: Soft iron magnetizes readily when current flows and loses most of that magnetism when current stops. These properties make the electromagnet easy to switch on and off. Steel retains more magnetism.
